newsitem.title: FRANCE: TF1 head sees top place for TPS in digital pay TV.
newsitem.headline: TF1 head sees top place for TPS in digital pay TV.

text.p: Television Par Satellite (TPS) will be the leader in French digital pay-TV by the end of 1998, Patrick Le Lay, chairman of both TPS and private terrestrial channel TF1, said on Wednesday.
He told a parliamentary committee that TPS, launched last December, would have 100,000 subscribers by the end of March and would bring its owners a "gigantic" return on capital.
"By the end of March we will have 100,000 subscribers. I cannot give a figure for the whole of 1997, but by the end of 1998, we will be the leader of digital pay television," he said.
"TPS will be a major financial success on the investment front," he said.

Last week TPS managing director Cyrille Peloux predicted the digital satellite station would have over 250,000 subscribers by the end of this year, of whom 150,000 would be signed up by the end of June.
He said that 25,000 of the 80,000 subscribers TPS has signed up so far had now received their decoders, and a logjam in supplying these would be over by May.
TPS competes with Canalsatellite, a subsidiary of pay-TV group Canal Plus, which also launched its digital satellite TV service last December.

TPS is controlled by private terrestrial channel M6-Metropole TV and its parents, Lyonnaise des Eaux and CLT, controlled by Belgian financier Albert Frere's Audiofina. TF1 and France Telecom each have 25 percent.
